description: Backend: persist and merge user-uploaded deployment plans. Add a new DynamoDB table for user plans, make the plan registry (deployment_plans.py) merge built-in static plans with user plans, add API routes to create/list/delete user plans (compose content stored to the S3 compose bucket, metadata to the table), and make the deployer resolve composeFile+modelName from the plan record for dynamic plans. This is a single coherent backend unit: registry + API handler + deployer + models, all Python. CDK wiring (table, route, IAM, env) is FEAT-002 and must be applied for this to run in AWS, but the Python code is self-contained and validated by ast.parse here.
steps: In platform/lambda/api/models.py: extend the DeploymentPlan dataclass with a field `source: str = "builtin"` (values 'builtin' or 'user'). Keep to_dict() returning all fields. Do not break existing built-in constructions (they omit source, so default 'builtin' applies).

In platform/lambda/api/deployment_plans.py: add a DynamoDB-backed dynamic layer. Read table name from env DEPLOYMENT_PLAN_TABLE (default 'TpotDeploymentPlanTable'). Add a helper _get_user_plans() that scans the table and returns a list of dicts (each item already has id,name,instanceType,composeFile,recipe,description,modelName,source='user'); tolerate ClientError by returning []. Update get_all_plans() to return built-in plan dicts (each with source='builtin') PLUS user plan dicts, with user plans NOT overriding a built-in of the same id (built-ins win; skip user dup ids). Update get_plan(plan_id) to check built-ins first, then look up the user plan by planId via get_item and return an object exposing .instanceType and .to_dict() (either construct a DeploymentPlan from the item or return the built-in DeploymentPlan). Ensure create_booking in handler.py still works: it reads plan.instanceType and get_all_plans()[i]['id'].

In platform/lambda/api/handler.py: add three handler functions. create_deployment_plan(body): validate required fields name (1-100 chars) and instanceType (must be in an allowlist ALLOWED_INSTANCE_TYPES = the set of instanceTypes used by built-ins today: 'p5en.48xlarge','p6-b300.48xlarge' - define as a module constant and allow extending) and composeContent (non-empty string). Parse composeContent with a YAML check: since PyYAML may not be bundled, first try `import yaml; yaml.safe_load` inside try/except ImportError and if unavailable fall back to a minimal structural check (non-empty, contains 'services' or top-level mapping) - document this. Derive planId by slugifying name (lowercase, [a-z0-9-] only, collapse repeats) and reject if it collides with a built-in id or an existing user planId unless body has overwrite=true. Sanitize composeFile name = f'user-{planId}.yaml' (no path separators, no ..). Reject composeContent larger than 512 KB. Write compose content to S3: bucket from env COMPOSE_BUCKET, key f'compose-files/{composeFile}', ContentType text/yaml. Persist metadata to the plan table: {planId,name,instanceType,composeFile, recipe (default 'recipes/b300-pd-hold.env' - keep same default built-ins use, or accept from body), description (from body or ''), modelName (from body or 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash'), source:'user', createdAt}. Return 201 with the stored plan. Return 400 on validation failure, 409 on id collision without overwrite.

In platform/lambda/api/handler.py: add list_deployment_plans() returning {'plans': get_all_plans()} (200), and delete_deployment_plan(plan_id) that refuses to delete a built-in (404/400), deletes the S3 object compose-files/<composeFile> (best-effort) and the DynamoDB item, returns 200. Reuse the existing _response helper.

In platform/lambda/api/handler.py router: add branches - resource '/deployment-plans' + POST -> create_deployment_plan(body); '/deployment-plans' + GET -> list_deployment_plans(); '/deployment-plans/{planId}' + DELETE -> delete_deployment_plan(path_params.get('planId','')). Read COMPOSE_BUCKET and DEPLOYMENT_PLAN_TABLE from os.environ near the other env constants at the top of handler.py. Add a _get_plan_table() helper mirroring _get_booking_table().

In platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py: make _handle_deploy resolve composeFile and modelName for dynamic plans. After computing plan_compose_map.get(deployment_plan) and PLAN_MODEL_MAP.get(deployment_plan): if the plan id is NOT in plan_compose_map (i.e. a user plan), read the plan record from DynamoDB (env DEPLOYMENT_PLAN_TABLE default 'TpotDeploymentPlanTable', get_item Key={'planId': deployment_plan}) and use its composeFile and modelName. Fall back to existing defaults if the record is missing. Add a small _get_plan_record(plan_id) helper. Keep behavior identical for built-in plan ids.

Validate every changed Python file with: python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('<file>').read())" for platform/lambda/api/handler.py, platform/lambda/api/deployment_plans.py, platform/lambda/api/models.py, platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py.
acceptance_criteria: ast.parse succeeds on handler.py, deployment_plans.py, models.py (api) and deployer/handler.py.
get_all_plans() returns built-in plans each carrying source='builtin' and merges user plans (source='user') without built-ins being overridden by same-id user plans.
get_plan(id) returns an object with .instanceType and .to_dict() for both built-in and user plan ids, and None for unknown ids (so create_booking's 'Invalid deployment plan' path is preserved).

POST /deployment-plans validates name+instanceType(allowlist)+composeContent, sanitizes planId/filename, rejects >512KB and id collisions (without overwrite), writes compose to s3://COMPOSE_BUCKET/compose-files/<file> and metadata to the plan table, returns 201.
GET /deployment-plans returns merged plans; DELETE /deployment-plans/{planId} refuses built-ins and removes user plan S3 object + table item.
Deployer resolves composeFile+modelName from the DynamoDB plan record for a user plan id and is unchanged for built-in ids.
verification: Read-through review: confirm router branches exist for the three new routes and that env constants COMPOSE_BUCKET + DEPLOYMENT_PLAN_TABLE are read in both api/handler.py and deployer/handler.py.
review_response_2026-09-03: Addressed review 2026-09-03-073602 (NEEDS_CHANGES) backend items. Issue 1 (YAML validation near-no-op): tightened _validate_compose_content in platform/lambda/api/handler.py. It still prefers yaml.safe_load when importable, but now requires the parsed doc to be a non-empty mapping WITH a dict `services` section (not just any non-empty dict). The PyYAML-absent fallback was rewritten into a new helper _fallback_has_services_mapping() that requires a real top-level `services:` block: either block form (a line `services:` at column 0 followed by at least one indented, non-blank/non-comment child before the next top-level key) or non-empty inline mapping form (`services: {...}`, rejecting `{}`), instead of the old 'contains substring services OR any line with a colon' check. Confirmed the API Lambda is packaged via lambda.Code.fromAsset('./lambda/api') with NO bundling/pip step in platform/lib/tpot-booking-stack.ts, so the dependency-free structural fallback (not adding PyYAML) is the correct fix; documented this in the docstrings. Issue 3 (orphaned S3 object on failed metadata write): in create_deployment_plan, the put_item failure path now best-effort deletes the S3 compose object (compose-files/user-<planId>.yaml) before returning 500, logging a warning if cleanup also fails. Kept S3-first ordering + the 500 response. Issue 4 (recipe accepted but unused): kept accepting/persisting recipe (built-in plan records also carry a recipe field, so removing it would make user rows inconsistent) and added a code comment documenting it is reserved for future deployer use. VALIDATION: python3 ast.parse + py_compile pass on handler.py (Python 3.9 host; Lambda is 3.12). Ran a throwaway script (since deleted) that exec'd handler.py with stubbed boto3/models/etc and asserted _fallback_has_services_mapping + _validate_compose_content on 11 cases (valid block/inline pass; no-services, random colon text, empty-services-then-top-key, services-with-no-child, empty inline {}, commented services, empty string all correctly fail) - ALL PASS. On the 3.9 host PyYAML is absent so this exercised the exact Lambda fallback path. CDK synth / frontend build deferred (no node/npm on host). Did NOT commit.
